Interactive map shows dozens of reported sightings as Derby remains among most haunted UK cities

Every location where a ghost has been sighted appears on our interactive map

14:06, 31 Oct 2026

Derbyshire is full of ghostly sightings and grim tales from years gone by - and what better way to celebrate Halloween weekend than by delving into these paranormal activities.

‌

‌

Author Dr Paul Lee has documented more than 5,500 reported hauntings around the country over a decade of painstaking research, and you can use our interactive map to see Derbyshire's most haunted locations.

‌

Many of our tales surround pubs and old buildings around Derby city centre - but delve up north towards the Peak District, and you'll see cloaked figures roaming natural and man-made 17th-century rock features, or even a spirit of a little boy patiently waiting by an old well.

‌

You can read about more than 100 cases across Derbyshire - with around 40 of these coming from Derby itself.

Other ghoulish hotspots include Chesterfield, with around 20 locations, Ashover, with five and Bakewell, also with five.

Take a deep dive into Derbyshire's most haunted locations below:

‌

According to Dr Lee’s research, Britain’s most haunted postcode is the ME1 neighbourhood, which covers Rochester, Burham, and Wouldham in Kent.

‌

Paranormal experiences have been documented at more than 50 separate locations across these Medway communities.

Among them is the former Royal Function Rooms, an 18th-century theatre that closed in 2022. The venue was long said to be haunted by three separate spectres.

‌

They include an aggressive figure in an 18th-century waistcoat who allegedly ran across the stage overturning furniture, a second shouting phantom, and a woman in a bonnet who was reported to rattle door handles in the basement.

York city centre (YO1) is the UK’s second most haunted postcode, famous for its ghost walks - although many in Derby claim our city to be just as active. One of York's most chilling tales centres on St Saviour Church, where a "grey lady" is reputed to walk at midnight.

‌

Local folklore tells of an amateur ghost hunter who spent the night locked inside the church, only to be discovered the following morning either dead with his face a “mask of terror”, or scared out of his senses, depending on the retelling.

All the descriptions of paranormal activity on the map have come from Dr Lee’s research, which, in many cases, includes interviews with witnesses and his own investigations, during which he has visited numerous locations and studied various newspaper archives.

Dr Lee said: "Of course, some of the reports in the database could be hoaxes or urban legends; there is no way to know in many cases."
